dedupe_keys.name: china s coal methane emissions over 2011 2019 gridded inventory

description: This dataset is a gridded inventory of methane emissions from China's coal mines for 2011 to 2019, split into abandoned mine methane and underground coal mine methane, with the source data and the code used for the emission and uncertainty calculations. It was produced by Qiang Liu, Fei Teng, Chris P. Nielsen, Yuzhong Zhang and Lixin Wu to quantify coal methane at mine scale, including the rarely inventoried emissions of closed mines. Files are GeoTIFF rasters for selected years (2011, 2015, 2017 and 2019 for the two categories), an Excel workbook of source data and a Python script, each raster about 0.3 MB, published on 19 March 2024 as a free Zenodo download under CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: the grid spacing and methods are documented in the associated article, not the record, and emissions are estimates from activity data and emission factors, not measurements. For simulation it shows where active and abandoned coal mines sit and how intensively they emit, useful for environmental impact scenarios, mine closure planning and exposure of surrounding assets to gas hazards. Related catalogue records include the Global Coal Mine Tracker and the coal mine methane inventory for India and Australia.
